faq_1_question: What is EU Duty Drawback and how can it reduce my customs costs?
faq_1_answer: EU Duty Drawback is a customs recovery mechanism that enables you to reclaim <strong>100% of duties, taxes, and fees</strong> paid when importing goods that are subsequently exported or destroyed. For retail brands, this translates to recovering expenses on <strong>customer returns sent back internationally</strong>. This directly enhances your landed cost profitability and working capital.
faq_2_question: Can non-EU brands claim Duty Drawback on returned goods exported from the EU?
faq_2_answer: <strong>Yes</strong>, if you meet three conditions: (1) You were the <strong>importer</strong> when the goods entered the EU, (2) TDR cleared goods into the EU using its <strong>proprietary</strong> clearance process, and (3) the returned goods were imported and the drawback claim was sbubmitted within <strong>3 monts</strong> after importation. Many non-EU brands overlook this. Returns can generate <strong>6-8% cost savings</strong> on original import duties.
faq_3_question: Can EU brands exporting inventory that was previously imported benefit from duty free solutions?
faq_3_answer: <p>If you import goods into the EU and later export them <strong>unused</strong> to consignees (e.g., distributors, subsidiaries), you can avoid paying for import duties by using a <strong>EU bonded warehouse</strong></br>The EU typically would not allow for B2B2C ecom orders to be amended</p>
faq_4_question: What documentation is critical for EU Duty Drawback claims?
faq_4_answer: <p>To put it simply, you'll need <strong>documentation and data</strong> supporting your <strong>import and export activities</strong>. This encompasses customs entry records and commercial invoices.<br /><br /><strong>The TDR Advantage:</strong> We provide full assistance in establishing a compliant documentation archive.</p>
faq_5_question: How long does it take to receive Duty Drawback refunds?
faq_5_answer: <p><strong>The EU customs authorities process claims in 3-5 months</strong> on average.<br /><br /><strong>The TDR Advantage:</strong> Our support team submit claims and handles customs enquiry online to minimise processing time.<br /><br /><strong>Finance teams</strong>: Plan for a 5<strong>-month working capital cycle</strong>but refunds are <strong>interest-free</strong>, so the ROI is effectively the full duty amount recovered.</p>
faq_6_question: What percentage of duties and fees can I recover?
faq_6_answer: <p><strong>100% of duties, taxes, and most fees</strong>. Claims must be submitted within 3 months after the initial importation date.</p>
faq_7_question: What are the top reasons Duty Drawback claims get rejected?
faq_7_answer: <p><strong>Avoid these mistakes</strong>: (1) <strong>Missing export proof</strong>(e.g., no MRN entry details, no commercial invoice...), (2) <strong>Inadequate inventory tracking</strong> (can't link imports to exports), (3) <strong>Late filings</strong> (3-months deadline from import), (4) <strong>Non compliant import clearance</strong>process, and (5) <strong>Using non-identical goods</strong>.<br /><br /><strong>The TDR Advantage:</strong> Our team will support you implementing a <strong>drawback-specific ERP workflow</strong> before claiming.</p>
faq_8_question: Should we file EU Duty Drawback claims in-house or use a customs broker?
faq_8_answer: <p><strong>DIY</strong>: Feasible if you have <strong>an EU approved customs software and robust customs expertise</strong>. <br /> Alternatively, <strong>TDR</strong> takes care of all the heavy lifting, the EDI connection with Customs and typically increases recovery rate by 30% through optimization.</p>
faq_9_question: Are there audit risks with Duty Drawback, and how can we mitigate them?
faq_9_answer: <p><strong>Yes</strong>. EU audits <strong>~5% of claims</strong> annually. <strong>Red flags</strong>: High claim volumes, frequent substitution use, or inconsistent documentation. <strong>Mitigation</strong>: (1) <strong>Conduct a pre-filing audit</strong> of your records, (2) <strong>Document everything</strong> (e.g., order tracing, reason for returns...), and (3) <strong>Designate a single POC</strong> for customs inquiries. <strong>Penalties</strong> for negligence can include <strong>denied claims</strong> or <strong>severe fines</strong>.<br><br><strong>The TDR Advantage:</strong> Trust our expert team to submit fully compliant claims to EU customs</strong> and reduce the risk of Customs audits.</p>
